next_step: Run a calibrated multi-clock stress test: collect endpoint probabilities and projected reaction activity at two or more observation-clock rates while checking that readout is noninvasive and physical kinetics remain unchanged. Analyze the observations jointly with the shared-clock hierarchy, starting at its lowest useful level.
allocation: One worker-unit audits clock/readout calibration and the unchanged-kinetics assumption; one designs and analyzes the multi-clock stress test.
decisive_observation: Whether calibrated observations across clocks are jointly compatible with the shared-clock constraints, and whether the finite-level feasible set narrows compared with separate one-clock fits.
outcome_decisions: If jointly incompatible, revisit the assumptions or reject the representation for this setting. If compatible and constraints narrow, continue the hierarchy analysis while retaining non-identifiability. If compatible but broad, prioritize the conditional hierarchy proof extension or a more informative clock design.
retained_result: Keep the proved one-clock endpoint and projected-activity characterization, and its homogeneous generator only as an occupation-weighted explanation for its specified clock. The binary example already shows that one-clock agreement does not identify a physical generator.
uncertainty: Finite-level constraints are outer bounds with no stated convergence rate; completeness is conditional on bounded observable activity and the stated clock, readout, and unchanged-kinetics assumptions. This test alone cannot establish the physical generator.
